newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were expected to open mostly higher Tuesday, with platinum group metals likely to climb further, but gold expected to remain weak.

NYMEX September palladium was called up $5.00 to $10.00 from Monday's close at a new contract high of $215.60 an ounce, after TOCOM palladium futures went limit up for the fifth straight day in Tokyo and after spot palladium fixed at a fresh 17-year high at $245.50 in London this morning.
NYMEX October platinum was called up the same from Tuesday's finish of $455.20.
NYMEX October platinum also saw a contract high Monday and platinum futures contracts also went limit up on TOCOM overnight.

Heavy shortcovering by Japanese traders which had built up a 50 tonne short position in palladium, along with a dearth of PGMs in the physical market and cointinued concerns about the reliability of Russian supplies were pushing PGM prices sharply higher, traders said.
COMEX September silver was called unchanged to up 0.30 cent from Monday's close of $4.507.
COMEX warehouse silver stocks rose 607,502 ounces Monday to 169,686,183 ounces, after falling to the lowest level Friday since the addition of Wilmington Trust stocks in January.
COMEX gold stocks rose 15,599 ounces to 929,610 ounces.
COMEX December gold was called unchanged to down $0.50 from the previous close of $328.10.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted early at $323.00/50 compared to the London morning fix of $323.35 and the New York close Monday of $323.65/$324.15.
Gold prices are still seen capped by the surging dollar which reached a new seven-year high against the mark overnight and set a fresh seven-year high on its trade-weighted index also.
